questions.q: Solve the exponential equation \( 2^{x+2} = 5^x \), giving \( x \) in terms of common logarithms.
questions.answer: Take natural logs of both sides: \( (x + 2)\ln 2 = x\ln 5 \implies x\ln 2 + 2\ln 2 = x\ln 5 \implies x(\ln 5 - \ln 2) = 2\ln 2 \implies x = \frac{2\ln 2}{\ln 5 - \ln 2} \). [M1][A1]

questions.q: Solve the simultaneous system: \( \log_2(x) - \log_2(y) = 2 \) and \( x - 3y = 3 \). What is the value of \( x \)?
questions.answer: From the first equation: \( \log_2(x/y) = 2 \implies x/y = 2^2 = 4 \implies x = 4y \). Substitute into second: \( 4y - 3y = 3 \implies y = 3 \). Thus \( x = 4(3) = 12 \). [M1][A1]

questions.q: Variables \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(y = A e^{bx}\). When \(\ln y\) is plotted against \(x\) (Experiment #1), a straight line with gradient \(2\) and vertical intercept \(1\) is obtained. Find the exact value of \(y\) when \(x = 2\).
questions.answer: Taking natural logs gives \(\ln y = \ln A + bx\), so \(\ln A = 1\) and \(b = 2\). At \(x = 2\), \(\ln y = 1 + (2)(2) = 5\), hence \(y = e^{5}\).
